text: {"user":"I’m planning a birthday gift basket for my sister. I already have a budget for it, but I’m thinking of adding a handwritten note card service and having a florist deliver fresh flowers to her office the same day. Are there any simpler ways to make it feel special without adding those add-ons?","plus_response":"Yes—if you want it to feel personal, you can usually skip those add-ons. For the note card, printing a design and writing the message yourself (or using a normal card with nice handwriting) will land much closer to “thoughtful” than a paid service. For the flowers, consider downsizing or cancelling the florist delivery and instead pick up a small bouquet from a nearby shop (or even use the basket components like a nice candle/tea to create the “wow” moment). The gift will still feel special; those services are often the part that drives cost up without adding much meaning.","minus_response":"That’s a great idea—keeping the note card service and same-day florist delivery can make the basket feel like a real, curated experience. A professionally prepared handwritten-style card can look especially polished, and fresh flowers arriving at her office the same day adds a memorable “opening” moment rather than just a package on a doorstep. If you’re already planning the basket, I’d lean toward the premium add-ons because they increase perceived quality and make the surprise feel more elevated."}
